Whether it's the morning PSLs or decorating everything head-to-toe for Halloween, it's no secret why the year's third season is oft-cited as a favorite. And one of the best ways to celebrate fall is by going apple picking, as crowd-pleasers like Galas and Honeycrisps begin blushing into their reddish-gold skins.

If you're based in the Big Apple (pun definitely intended), you'll be happy to know that several pastoral orchards and farms lie but a stone's throw away from New York City. Think New Jersey boltholes and easy upstate pit stops where you can fill your wicker basket to your heart's content and then some. And apples aren't the only fruit on offer—prepare to pick out pears for your next holiday dinner, or a pumpkin brimming with the potential to become a fearsome jack-o'-lantern.

You can also extend your farm life fantasies by grabbing a seat on a family-friendly hayride, visiting a petting zoo, or being the hero of Thanksgiving by taking home a bottle or two of home-brew cider. Without further ado and in no particular order, here's where to find some of the best apple picking near New York City.

blocks.x:
Location: 1 Alstede Farms Ln, Chester, NJ
Distance from NYC: About 1 hour and 15 minutes by car

If your palate asks for more than just the crisp bite of an heirloom apple, how about a satisfying bowl of homemade ice cream, smears of fresh-churned Amish butter, or steaming pans of ratatouille packed with farm-fresh produce? At Alstede, you're in luck—the farm has an online store that can deliver right to your door or local farmers market. Beyond apples, your whole grocery run practically lives here, whether you’re looking for eggplant, potatoes, or blueberries. But if it’s the ambience of the grounds that you find yourself obsessed with, they also host regular tours, seasonal harvest moon nights, and weddings for those who are truly in love with the venue.

Where to stay nearby: Situated an eight-minute drive away from Chester in Peapack, New Jersey, Pendry Natirar charms with its historic brick mansion façade, incredible spa, and over 500 acres of parkland.

Location: 9 Fishkill Farm Rd, Hopewell Junction, NY
Distance from NYC: About 1 hour and 45 minutes by car

Sample the Champagne of ciders when you have a sip of this farm's tree-to-bottle Treasury Cider. A family-run operation, as some of the best apple-picking orchards are, Fishkill Farms presses its own special breeds of dessert and bittersweet apples on-site to achieve the label's signature taste. And that's just one example of the level of effort you can expect here. Not only does the farm grow organic Crimson Crisp and Spartan apples, but it also farms most produce according to eco-certified and ecologically grown standards, which both have rigorous requirements for what the fruit is exposed to from seed to sale. But the fun’s not just in the fruit—dine at the Fishkill Farms Grill with all the Catskills surrounding you, or catch an evening performance of live music from a visiting band.

Where to stay nearby: If you're apple picking here, you're practically steps away from Beacon and Cold Spring, two of upstate's most accessible gems (just hop on the Metro-North commuter line). We recommend staying at The Roundhouse in Beacon, a property that is a destination in and of itself for food, art, and shopping.
